conviction_note: Nothing unpriced found: every positive driver (warm European summer, Eastern Europe comps fading, record OEM backlog, US AHRI shipment rebound, FX turning slightly positive) is already written into sell-side previews of about 3.5-4% organic growth and a Bloomberg bar of SEK 10,819m sales and SEK 1,208m EBIT. A record of small misses (EPS below consensus in 3 of the last 4 quarters; -6.0% and -5.4% on two of them) pulls p_up slightly under 50, so the scaled number is about zero on an abs move of 4.5%. The findings sum to -0.1 and agree with it.

already_public.what: No profit warning (vinstvarning) and no pre-release of Q3: the Nasdaq Nordic feed for Beijer Ref since the 17 July Q2 report carries only CEO changes and acquisitions

Q2 call (17 July): July sales positive; the Eastern Europe drag to fade by at least 50% in Q3 and be gone in Q4; OEM to keep growing double digits on a record backlog; North America 'still repair, replacement', no major improvement expected
Internal CEO appointment (Jonas Steen, starts 1 Nov); the acting CEO/CFO Joel Davidsson presents Q3 on 22 October
Acquisitions closed or signed since Q2: Refspecs (NZ), a Canadian HVAC distributor, Refra (Lithuania, consolidated from 9 Oct, so after Q3), a Greek HVAC distributor

new_in_release.expect: Q3 sales and EBITA are new, and the bar is about 3.5-4% organic. Lean very slightly toward in line or a touch above: Q3 2025 organic was +5% (NA +6.3%), which is a hard comparison, against Eastern Europe fading and strong OEM. Low confidence.
No formal guidance; Beijer gives none. Possible qualitative Q4 commentary from an acting CEO; unknown.
Q3 2025 operating cash flow was a very strong SEK 1,617m comparison; the late-Q2 receivables build should unwind in Q3. Direction unknown, a risk to the headline.
Net debt/EBITDA was 2.40 at Q2 and acquisitions continued, so leverage is probably flat to up; acquisition pipeline commentary likely positive.

bar: Bloomberg consensus via Finwire/Börsvärlden (2026-10-21): sales SEK 10,819m (10 estimates), EBIT SEK 1,208m (8 estimates) against 9,726 / 1,079 a year earlier, https://borsvarlden.com/artiklar/beijer-ref-vantas-redovisa-1-208-miljoner-kronor-i-rorelseresultat-bloomberg. Roughly agrees with SB1 Markets' adjusted EBITA estimate of SEK 1,273m, said to be 1.1% above consensus (implying about 1,259m) and +3.6% organic (secondary aggregator: https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/nebenwerte/sb1-markets-lifts-target-for-beijer-ref-stock-to-sek-200-00/70331510), and with Nordea's 'cirka 4 procent' organic, https://www.placera.se/telegram/beijer-ref-nordea-hojer-riktkursen-for-beijer-ref-till-182-kronor-upprepar-kop-20261009. Sourced and two sources agree; there is no company guidance.

That is the truncation floor and not a measurement (anchor_covered false), so building or covering is unknown. findings.finding: AHRI reports US central AC and heat-pump shipments up 20.1% y/y in July 2026 and 11.4% in August, after +21.7% in June: a rebound across Q3 in Beijer's North American end market, about 24% of group sales.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: North America organic +6.3% in Q3 2025 (stock +0.9% on the day) and -2.9% in Q2 2026 (stock +0.8%); the stock has not visibly traded on the NA line alone.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the series is public (July data out 11 Sep, August 12 Oct) and the previews already carry +3.5-4% organic. It is OEM sell-in against a 2025 destocking base, not distributor sell-through. Beijer's own NA comparison is a hard +6.3%, and management said on 17 July it saw no major NA improvement. If the market had read it as a large NA upside, the stock would not be down 1% over 20 days.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call management said July sales were positive, the Eastern Europe (Cool4U) drag would fade by at least 50% in Q3, and OEM (Fenagy, SCM Frigo) backlog runs 'well into 2027' with double-digit growth expected.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 organic +1% with OEM +25%: stock +0.8%. Q1 2026 organic -0.2%: stock -6.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is the company's own public steer, and Nordea's +4% organic call ('Efter den varma sommaren i Europa väntas den organiska tillväxten nå cirka 4 procent') shows the sell-side built it in. It lands inside what the company said, so it is near zero.

findings.finding: Board open-market buying after Q2: chair Per Bertland bought 10,000 B shares and director Joen Magnusson 8,000 on 2026-08-19 (FI insynsregister: 'Förvärv').
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observable prior reaction to insider buys on this name.
findings.original_quote: Per Bertland | Styrelseordförande | Förvärv | Beijer Ref AB ser. B | 2026-08-19 | 10 000 (chair, acquisition, 10,000 B shares)
findings.why_not_priced: Small (about SEK 1.4m for the chair), two months old and public in the register, bought before Q3 had ended. A weak signal at most.

findings.finding: Cash-flow comparison risk: Q3 2025 operating cash flow was a record SEK 1,617m, against SEK 293m in Q2 2026 (635) after a late-quarter receivables build, with net debt/EBITDA up to 2.40 (2.10) and acquisitions continuing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 'strong cash flow' headline: +0.9%. Q2 2026 weaker OCF inside a record quarter: +0.8%. Cash has not been decisive here before.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews quoted in the press focus on sales and EBIT; none of the sourced previews gives a cash-flow bar. But the Q2 receivables built because sales came late in the quarter, so they should be collected in Q3. The sign is genuinely uncertain, hence small.

findings.finding: Leadership change: the CEO quit in July, and the internal COO EMEA Jonas Steen was named CEO on 19 Oct, starting 1 Nov. The stock fell 1.3% that day and 2.1% the next. The acting CEO/CFO presents Q3.
findings.original_quote: Joel Davidsson kommer att presentera bolagets delårsrapport för det tredje kvartalet 2026 den 22 oktober (Joel Davidsson will present the Q3 2026 interim report on 22 October)
findings.why_not_priced: Priced: announced two sessions before the print and already traded on. Any strategy change from the new CEO lands after 1 Nov. A caretaker presenter makes a kitchen-sink or new targets unlikely, so this adds no sign.

findings.finding: A record of small misses with outsized negative reactions: EPS was below consensus in 3 of the last 4 quarters (Q4-25 -9.3%, Q1-26 -1.1%, Q2-26 -3.7%). Confirmed report-day moves: Q2-26 +0.8, Q1-26 -6.0 (EBIT 746 vs 749 est), Q4-25 -5.4, Q3-25 +0.9, Q2-25 +1.5, Q1-25 +6.2, Q4-24 -0.5, Q3-24 -4.2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A 0.4% EBIT miss in Q1-26 produced -6.0%; an in-line Q2-26 produced +0.8%.
findings.original_quote: Kursutveckling vid senaste rapporterna ... Q2-2026 2026-07-17 0,8 / Q1-2026 2026-04-23 -6,0 / Q4-2025 2026-01-30 -5,4 (share-price move on the last report days)
findings.why_not_priced: It is a reaction pattern, not a fact about Q3: the market punishes small misses here. Consensus EPS of about 1.62 (+12.5% y/y) asks for a step-up from Q2's +5%, which leaves room for another small miss. It is weak evidence, so it is held small.

baseline_tension: Agrees with a near-zero lean (priced_lean +0.05, 20-day run-up -1.0%, 5-day -3.0% after the CEO news): there is nothing to beat and nothing found against it.
language_note: Finwire/Börsvärlden (Swedish) carried the Bloomberg consensus table (sales 10,819, EBIT 1,208, the estimate counts) and the confirmed report-day reaction history with real dates. That history corrects the baseline's cadence-estimated dates, several of which miss the true report days by up to three weeks.
Placera/Finwire (Swedish) carried Nordea's Q3 organic call of about 4% on the warm European summer; English aggregators carried only the target-price change.
FI's Swedish insynsregister carried the board's August share purchases.
The issuer's own releases are bilingual and identical in content; nothing in the Swedish filings adds to the English ones.
lessons_applied: A narrow proxy and macro-to-company transmission (AHRI sell-in against the company's own cautious NA comment and a +6.3% comparison): AHRI finding cut from +0.3 to +0.2.
A finding that lands inside what the company already said: the Q2-call Q3 commentary cut from +0.2 to +0.1.
Insider buys are two months old and small: cut from +0.2 to +0.1.

'Too small about the move' / reaction history moves p_up, not abs_move: abs_move_pct raised from 4.0 to 4.5 (numbers are new, no guide; confirmed report-day moves include -6.0, -5.4, +6.2, -4.2), and the miss-prone reaction pattern moves p_up from 50 to 48.
'Cash can outweigh': the cash-flow comparison finding kept at -0.2 as a named line rather than dropped.
